definitions.explanation: A formal name or title used to refer to a person, place, or thing. More formal and official than ordinary naming. Often used in institutional, academic, or regulatory contexts when discussing what something is officially called.

examples.japanese: {正式|せいしき}な{呼称|こしょう}は{何|なん}ですか。
この{役職|やくしょく}の{呼称|こしょう}が{変更|へんこう}された。
examples.english: The title of this position was changed.

examples.japanese: {各国|かっこく}で{同|おな}じ{製品|せいひん}でも{呼称|こしょう}が{異|こと}なることがあるため、{国際的|こくさいてき}な{統一|とういつ}が{求|もと}められている。
examples.english: Since the same product can have different designations in different countries, international standardization is being called for.

notes:
USAGE:
{呼称|こしょう} is a formal word used for official or institutional names and titles. It is more formal than {呼|よ}び{方|かた} (casual way of calling) and {名前|なまえ} (name). Common in bureaucratic, academic, and business writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {正式|せいしき}{呼称|こしょう}: official designation
- {呼称|こしょう}を{変更|へんこう}する: to change the designation
- {呼称|こしょう}が{異|こと}なる: to have different designations
- {一般的|いっぱんてき}な{呼称|こしょう}: common designation
